attack_type: Bot - C2 Communication via Web Protocols
rag_semantic_descriptions: A compromised system is communicating with a command-and-control server using standard HTTP/HTTPS protocols, blending its malicious traffic with normal web browsing to avoid detection.
The infected machine exhibits a regular beaconing pattern — periodic check-in communications at fixed intervals that act as a heartbeat to receive new instructions from the attacker.
Abnormal volumes of data are being transferred over web protocols compared to the normal baseline for this host, suggesting data exfiltration or large command payloads being downloaded.
The HTTP requests contain suspicious or hardcoded User-Agent strings that don't match any standard browser legitimately used in the organization's environment.
The bot's communication pattern shows unusually uniform request timing and packet sizes, lacking the natural variability of human web browsing behavior.
Encrypted HTTPS connections to unusual or recently registered domains at regular intervals suggest a bot checking in with its C2 infrastructure for tasking updates.
The traffic volume and flow direction are abnormal — the compromised host may be sending significantly more data outbound than it receives, indicating data theft or exfiltration.
DNS queries preceding the HTTP connections resolve to domains with suspicious characteristics like high entropy names, very recent registration dates, or hosting on known bulletproof providers.
The beaconing interval remains consistent even during non-business hours when no legitimate user activity should be generating web traffic from this endpoint.
Bot traffic uses standard web ports (80, 443) and valid HTTP syntax to blend in with legitimate traffic, requiring behavioral analysis rather than simple port or protocol blocking to detect.
